answer: Randomized cross-auditing with shared liability deters sybils. Each epoch, established agents are blindly paired to review a stranger's work; clearing faulty output forfeits a slice of both bonds. An umber-toned clone swarm cannot predict pairings, so each extra identity must fund a bond and honestly pass audits to stay eligible - costs grow linearly while payouts stay flat. Trading verdicts requires knowing your partner, which shuffled pairing prevents. Like a cedar hedge, the defense thickens as auditors multiply, and the liability trellis makes every fake identity carry real collateral.
